teaching.hint: After one move, what probability is at each on-board square, and what happens to probability assigned to off-board choices?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The knight's future depends only on its current square and move count; survival probability can be propagated as mass over board cells rather than enumerating move sequences.
solution_outline.approach: Start with probability one at the initial square. For each of k moves, distribute every on-board square's current probability equally across all eight knight offsets, keeping only on-board destinations. Sum the remaining mass after the last layer.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: After t layers, each square stores exactly the probability of being there after t moves without ever having left the board; discarded mass represents paths that already ended off-board.
solution_outline.correctness: The initial layer matches the starting position. Each move independently chooses every one of eight offsets with probability one eighth, so distributing and summing mass computes every on-board arrival probability exactly. By induction, the final total is the probability of surviving all k attempted moves.
solution_outline.complexity: O(k n^2) time and O(n^2) auxiliary space with two board layers; each cell has eight constant-size transitions.
solution_outline.pitfall: Renormalizing among legal on-board moves is wrong: off-board choices remain possible and their probability must be lost.

accepted_alternatives: Memoized recursion on position and moves remaining computes the same probability in O(k n^2) time and O(k n^2) space.
common_wrong_turns: Forget that k=0 has probability one
source_fidelity_notes: The image of knight movement was replaced by exact coordinate offsets; uniform choice including off-board moves, early stopping, k=0, and bounds were retained.
